title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. G = π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. A larger group, written Π̂_{0,3} (with some tilde/hat decoration in the manuscript), contains G with index 3, or is an extension by the S_3-symmetries. In it, σ_∞ is the involution z ↦ 1−z (fixing ∞, exchanging 0 and 1) and ρ is the order-3 rotation of {0,1,∞}. An automorphism u of G, compatible with these symmetries, is encoded by cocycles g and h, roughly u(ρ) = gρ and u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞. These satisfy g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1 and h σ_∞(h) = 1. The previous page trivialises them: g = α ρ(α)^{-1} and h = β σ_∞(β)^{-1}, with lacets α, β in the bigger group. It also records a key dissymmetry. β always lies in π̂_{0,3}, but α lies in π̂_{0,3} only when ν ≡ 0 (mod 3), i.e. μ ≡ 1 (mod 3), where μ = 2ν+1 is the multiplier (cyclotomic-type character). There, u' = int(β^{-1})u gives h' = 1, so u is conjugate, modulo inner automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}, to an automorphism commuting with σ_∞.

This page. First it finishes that statement: the u' with u'(σ_∞) = σ_∞ is unique. Then it does the symmetric step u'' = int(α^{-1})u, giving (17): g'' = 1, h'' = (α^{-1}β) σ_∞(α^{-1}β)^{-1}, f'' = fα. In general u'' is only conjugate to u under the bigger group Π̂. It is conjugate under π̂_{0,3} to an automorphism commuting with ρ iff g is π̂-ρ-conjugate to 1. That holds iff α ∈ π̂_{0,3}, iff μ ≡ 1 (3), iff ν ≡ 0 (3).

Grothendieck then recalls that the earlier §§ treated the case h = 1 (u commutes with σ_∞). Once μ (equivalently ν) is known, the remaining data g and f determine each other via relation (11), with f viewed in L\π̂_{0,3}. He proposes to rewrite the equation in g as an equation in f, or better in φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1}, labelled (12). Note that φ σ_∞(φ) = 1 holds automatically.

The next page completes this. With ξ = l_0^ν φ, the condition becomes ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1. So outer automorphisms commuting with σ_∞, with multiplier μ = 2ν+1, correspond to pairs satisfying φ σ_∞(φ) = 1 and ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, linked by ξ = l_0^ν φ, with u recovered from f.

These are exactly Drinfeld's 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations defining GT^ (Drinfeld 1990; Ihara). The parameters correspond as λ ↔ μ and m = (λ−1)/2 ↔ ν. So the page is part of Grothendieck's independent, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the hexagonal and 2-cycle relations. Its specific content is the normalisation step: one can always conjugate to commute with the order-2 symmetry σ_∞, but with the order-3 symmetry ρ only when μ ≡ 1 mod 3.
errors: Line 'u'' sera seulement ...-conjugué de u''' must mean 'conjugué de u' (u'' conjugate to u); this is a slip, or a misreading in the transcription.

The criterion 'g est Π_{0,3}-ρ-conjugué à 1' should refer to the small group π̂_{0,3} (conjugation by elements of the index-3 subgroup), consistent with the conclusion 'ssi α ∈ π̂_{0,3}'. The notation for the two groups is inconsistent on the page.

The uniqueness claim 'un unique u′' with u′(σ_∞) = σ_∞ is not justified on this page. It needs the centraliser of σ_∞ in π̂_{0,3} to be trivial (modulo the relevant normaliser), which is plausible for this free profinite group but not argued here.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with the S_3-symmetries by cocycles g, h (u(ρ) = gρ, u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞), trivialising them as coboundaries αρ(α)^{-1} and βσ(β)^{-1}, and normalising by inner automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT^ elements / nonabelian cohomology of Z/2 and Z/3 acting on F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990-91); Lochak–Schneps for the S_3-symmetric viewpoint
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT-type group); the detailed computations are in La Longue Marche / these notes

ideas.what: Dissymmetry criterion: u can always be conjugated (by π̂_{0,3}) to commute with σ_∞, but to commute with ρ only iff the multiplier μ ≡ 1 mod 3 (ν ≡ 0 mod 3).
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction tied to the cyclotomic character mod 3, i.e. to the field of definition Q(√−3) of the fixed points of the order-3 symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on GT and S_3-/PSL_2(Z)-symmetry (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura); not clearly isolated in this form

ideas.what: Reducing the commuting-with-σ_∞ case to the pair of equations φσ_∞(φ) = 1 and ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1, with ξ = l_0^ν φ and ν = (μ−1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's relations (I) and (II) defining GT^, with m = (λ−1)/2

missed.claim: The mod-3 condition for simultaneously normalising against the order-3 symmetry ρ is the group-theoretic shadow of an arithmetic fact. The fixed points of ρ (primitive 6th roots of unity) are defined over Q(ζ_3), while those of σ_∞ (1/2 and ∞) are rational. So a GT^/Galois element can be normalised to commute with ρ iff its cyclotomic character is ≡ 1 mod 3. Grothendieck finds the obstruction 'μ ≡ 1 (3)' purely group-theoretically and names it 'la dissymétrie principale', without stating its arithmetic interpretation.
missed.quote: sera Π̂_{0,3}-conjugué à un élément qui commute à ρ ssi g est Π_{0,3}-ρ-conjugué à 1 i.e. ssi α∈Π̂_{0,3} i.e. ssi μ≡1 (3) ou encore ν≡0 (3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an explicit early formulation of how the PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3 symmetry interacts with GT^ and the cyclotomic character. This is relevant to orbifold/elliptic-point versions of GT and to Galois actions on π_1 of M_{1,1}-type orbifolds, and documents Grothendieck's priority on the normalisation analysis.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is part of Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld derivation of the GT^ relations, with ν = (μ−1)/2 matching Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2. That historical fact is partly known through the Longue Marche, so it is not shocking. The explicit mod-3 normalisation dissymmetry between σ_∞ and ρ is a nice unpublished detail, but the page itself is mostly routine conjugation bookkeeping.

Line 'g est Π_{0,3}-ρ-conjugué à 1' probably means conjugation by the small group π̂_{0,3}.
Left margin reads approximately: 'On a vu que μ est déterminé par f [à un signe près] dès la donnée de signes [?], cf plus bas'; the reading is uncertain.
